## Natural history notes

A medium-sized freshwater catfish characterized by a rounded head, yellowish to olive-brown body, pale belly, dark chin barbels, and a squared to slightly rounded tail. In Florida, it is found in ponds, lakes, slow rivers, canals, ditches, marshes, and backwaters, especially in areas with muddy bottoms, vegetation, woody debris, or low-flow conditions. It is an opportunistic bottom-feeder, using its barbels to locate insects, crustaceans, mollusks, small fish, plant material, and carrion, and males guard nests and young during the breeding season.
